title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: manage workforce requests from Microsoft 365 Copilot chat
summary: The briefing passes: its workforce request capabilities, security boundaries and roadmap dates are supported. The administrator path and Dataverse role-assignment call are documented, and the remaining feature-specific licensing and arrival-default gaps are stated narrowly.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes WEM integration with Microsoft 365 Copilot through MCP tools.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 Workforce Engagement Management (WEM) integrates with Microsoft 365 Copilot through Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.

claims.where: front matter: products; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap products are Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) and Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Dynamics 365 Customer Service"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is July CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability as a release phase.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap also lists Preview as a release phase.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap says organisations need not configure a separate permissions framework for these tools.
claims.quote: The integration uses the existing permission model, so organizations don't need to configure a separate permissions framework for these tools

claims.claim: Supervisors and representatives can list time-off, shift-swap and shift-bid requests in chat.
claims.quote: List and filter time-off, shift swap, and shift bid requests. Results are scoped to the user's role.

claims.claim: Supervisors and representatives can open individual workforce requests to review their details.
claims.quote: Retrieve the full record for a specific time-off, shift swap, or shift bid request.

claims.claim: Supervisors with reviewer permission can approve or reject pending time-off requests.
claims.quote: They can filter pending requests, inspect the details and scheduling context for an individual request, and approve or reject time-off requests when they have the required reviewer permission.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing Dynamics 365 and Dataverse security govern access to WEM tools and requests.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 and Dataverse security govern access to WEM MCP tools. Tool responses are limited to the records and actions the signed-in user is authorized to access.

claims.claim: The WEM catalog offers list_wem_requests, get_wem_request_details and decide_wem_time_off_request.
claims.quote:
`list_wem_requests` | List workforce requests
`get_wem_request_details` | Get request details
`decide_wem_time_off_request` | Approve or reject time-off requests

claims.claim: Representatives and supervisors do not typically use MCP tools directly.
claims.quote: Customer service representatives and supervisors don't typically use MCP tools directly. Instead, they interact with Service Agent.

claims.claim: Service Agent selects the appropriate tool.
claims.quote: Service Agent determines which tool to use, invokes it in the background, and presents the result in the conversation.

claims.claim: Service Agent invokes the tool in the background.
claims.quote: Service Agent determines which tool to use, invokes it in the background, and presents the result in the conversation.

claims.claim: Service Agent presents the tool result in the conversation.
claims.quote: Service Agent determines which tool to use, invokes it in the background, and presents the result in the conversation.

claims.quote: These tools connect a conversational experience, such as Service Agent, with Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Dataverse

claims.claim: list_wem_requests is read-only.
claims.quote: No, listing requests doesn't change data.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the feature-specific arrival default for the WEM tools.
claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 WEM MCP tools default enabled administrator switch; WEM MCP default tools enabled. Read roadmap, WEM overview and three tool pages, Service Agent FAQ, enablement and experience configuration; no WEM-specific arrival default.

claims.claim: Service Agent itself requires administrator configuration before use.

claims.claim: list_wem_requests defaults to team scope.
claims.quote: `scope` | `self` or `team`. Defaults to `team`—everything you can access.

claims.claim: With no request-type filter, listing includes every request type the caller can access.
claims.quote: When `requestType` is omitted, the tool returns all request types (time-off, shift-swap, shift-bid)

claims.claim: With no date filter, listing covers all dates.
claims.quote: when neither `from` nor `to` is supplied, the tool applies no date filter (all dates)

claims.claim: With no status filter, listing covers all request statuses.
claims.quote: By default, it shows all requests you can access, of every type, across all dates and statuses.

claims.claim: The default result limit is 25.
claims.quote: `top` | Integer maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

claims.claim: The result limit is capped at 200 requests.
claims.quote: `top` | Integer maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

claims.claim: Team-scope listing relies on Dataverse and WEM security to restrict results.
claims.quote: for the default `scope: team`, it relies on Dataverse and WEM security to return only rows the caller can read.

claims.claim: Request detail cards can include notes.
claims.quote: Time-off requests—time-off type, whether it's a full day, the start and end of the time off, hours, and notes.

claims.claim: Request details can include review information.
claims.quote:
Shift-bid requests—the request's status, dates, and review information.
Shift-swap requests—the request's status, dates, and review information.

claims.claim: Time-off detail cards can include the time-off window.
claims.quote: the time-off window for a time-off request

claims.claim: Responses are limited to records and actions authorised for the signed-in user.
claims.quote: Tool responses are limited to the records and actions the signed-in user is authorized to access.

claims.claim: POST /api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref assigns a user security role.

POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref
{ "@odata.id":"[Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/roles(<role ID>)" }

Manage deployment at the app level. The package doesn't provide separate administrator targeting for individual Service components.
Blocking prevents installation and use and removes the app from users who already installed it.
